prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

A cell stack device includes a cell stack including a plurality of cells arranged, and a manifold configured to allow a reaction gas to be supplied to the plurality of cells. First end portions of the plurality of cells are fixed to the manifold with a sealing material. The plurality of cells each include: a supporting substrate extending in a length direction; an element portion including a fuel electrode, a solid electrolyte layer, and an air electrode layered on the supporting substrate; and an interlayer located between the solid electrolyte layer and the air electrode, extending to each of the first end portions of the plurality of cells, and having a porosity greater than a porosity of the solid electrolyte layer. The interlayer includes an exposed portion exposed from the air electrode at each of the first end portions of the plurality of cells and the sealing material provided on the exposed portion.

outputs.L4:
A cell stack device includes a plurality of electrochemical cells arranged in a stack and a manifold configured to distribute a reaction gas to the cells. Each cell includes a support body and a layered power-generation structure disposed on the support body. The layered structure comprises a fuel electrode, a solid electrolyte, an interlayer, and an air electrode. One end of each cell is fixed to the manifold by a sealing material so that the reaction gas supplied through the manifold is directed to the intended gas passages while leakage from the connection region is suppressed.

The interlayer has a higher porosity than the electrolyte and extends continuously toward the end of the cell fixed to the manifold. Near that end, the interlayer includes an exposed portion on which the air electrode is not formed. The sealing material covers and contacts this air-electrode-free exposed portion, thereby defining a sealing interface between the cell and the manifold.

By omitting the air electrode from the portion of the interlayer located within the sealing region, direct contact between the sealing material and the air electrode is avoided. The porous exposed interlayer provides a controlled surface for receiving the sealing material and helps establish a reliable seal around the fixed end of each cell. This arrangement improves the integrity and positional definition of the cell-to-manifold joint while allowing reaction gas to be supplied efficiently to the multiple cells of the stack.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract describing a cell stack device with multiple cells fixed to a reaction-gas manifold, emphasizing a porous interlayer exposed beneath a sealing material.
counterfactuals.output: A cell stack device includes a reaction-gas manifold and a plurality of cells fixed to the reaction-gas manifold. Each cell includes a cell body, a porous interlayer disposed between the cell body and the reaction-gas manifold, and a sealing material configured to seal a reaction-gas flow path communicating with the cell. At least a portion of the porous interlayer extends beyond, and is exposed beneath an outer edge of, the sealing material. The exposed portion of the porous interlayer permits discharge of gas from a region adjacent to the sealing material, thereby suppressing gas accumulation and reducing stress or degradation at a sealed joint between the cells and the reaction-gas manifold.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the key structural features of a solid oxide fuel cell stack in one concise paragraph using formal patent language.
counterfactuals.output: A solid oxide fuel cell stack comprises a plurality of electrochemical cells arranged in a stacked configuration, each cell including a solid oxide electrolyte disposed between an anode and a cathode, and electrically conductive interconnect plates positioned between adjacent cells to provide series electrical connection and to define respective fuel-gas and oxidant-gas flow passages. The stack further comprises gas distribution manifolds configured to deliver and exhaust the reactant gases, sealing members arranged to inhibit intermixing and leakage thereof, current-collecting members disposed at opposing ends of the stacked cells, and a compression structure configured to maintain electrical contact, sealing engagement, and mechanical integrity during high-temperature operation.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.output:
A cell stack includes:

- Multiple electrochemical cells, each having a first end and an air electrode.
- A manifold to which the first ends of the cells are joined and sealed by a sealant.
- A porous interlayer formed along each cell and extending to its first end.
- Near the first end, the porous interlayer is exposed from beneath or beyond the air electrode.
- The exposed portion of the porous interlayer directly contacts the sealant, creating a porous, compliant interface between the cell and the manifold seal.

counterfactuals.prompt: Convert these invention details into patent-specification prose: arranged electrochemical cells, a reaction-gas supply manifold, sealed cell ends, layered electrode and electrolyte elements, and a high-porosity interlayer with an exposed sealing portion.
counterfactuals.output:
An electrochemical apparatus includes a plurality of electrochemical cells arranged in a cell stack and a reaction-gas supply manifold configured to distribute a reaction gas to the electrochemical cells. Each electrochemical cell includes first and second end portions that are sealed to inhibit leakage of the reaction gas. The cells comprise layered electrode and electrolyte elements, including at least a first electrode layer, an electrolyte layer, and a second electrode layer arranged in a laminated configuration.

A high-porosity interlayer is disposed between adjacent layered elements and is configured to facilitate passage and distribution of the reaction gas. The high-porosity interlayer includes a sealing portion that extends beyond, or is otherwise exposed relative to, at least one of the layered electrode and electrolyte elements. A sealing material engages the exposed sealing portion to form a seal at an end of the corresponding electrochemical cell. The exposed sealing portion thereby provides a sealing interface while a remaining portion of the high-porosity interlayer remains available for gas transport within the cell.
